_comment: Shared fixture for tools/gazetteer/core/depth.py and core/depth.mjs, asserted by BOTH test suites so the two implementations cannot drift. The browser half runs this check on every keystroke in the inspector; the Python half runs it at promotion. If they ever disagree, the tool tells you a location is finished and the promotion path refuses it. Spec: design/location-depth.md. Cases are hand-written, not generated from either implementation.

cases.why: The depth-0 standard: a name, a kind, one line of purpose. This is real text from the first session (Signal Box), which is what the 70-word ceiling was measured to accommodate.

doc.name: Signal Box
doc.note: Timber-framed on a brick base, controlling every movement through the Transfer and out along the causeway. Two signalmen a shift and a kettle that is never off. They have the best view of the whole crossing, and by long habit they wave at children on the platform.

cases.why: A depth-0 entry that genuinely outgrew the rung. Real text (The Roadgate). Not incomplete -- mis-declared, so it reports overweight while still passing. Exactly ONE overweight note: at depth named the summary is the whole prose, and reporting the summary ceiling and the total ceiling separately would say the same thing twice.

doc.name: The Roadgate
doc.note: Both highway lanes onto the fortress island pass underneath it, through a concrete throat wide enough for two vehicles abreast and no more. Traffic slows to walking pace inside, which is the point: the ceiling is firing slits, and a barrier drops at either end independently. Drivers know the drill — window down, pass held up, engine off if asked. At shift change the queue runs back a quarter mile, and the second lane is shut far more often than anyone has ever explained.

cases.why: Nothing written at all. Name and kind are required at every depth, so both are missing alongside the summary.
A depth-0 entry carrying attachments it has no business having yet -- a playlist and an NPC on a warehouse. Complete, but mis-declared from the other direction.
A complete sketch: summary, player-facing description, one hook. No NPC file, no art, no playlist -- correctly not required at depth 1.

lore.summary: Where island passes are issued, renewed and refused.
lore.playerFacing: Three windows, one of which is always shut. The waiting bench seats eleven and is usually full.

hooks: A clerk will bend the rules for someone who is genuinely desperate, once.

cases.why: Declared a sketch but written as a bare line: the player-facing description and the hook are both owed.

doc.name: Wash House
doc.note: Coin-fed washers and a drying yard.

cases.why: Declared a scene with nothing but a sketch's content. Everything the scene bundle obliges is listed: GM notes, a second activity, an NPC, art, a playlist.

lore.summary: The concourse where the two rail systems meet and nobody may walk straight through.
lore.playerFacing: Benches, a tea stand, and a departures board listing the island services in a smaller column.

hooks: Somebody is being turned back at the barrier.

cases.why: A complete depth-2 scene, with the full bundle attached: two activities, an NPC file, its own art, its own playlist.

lore.summary: A long shed beside the barrier where bags are opened on trestle tables.
lore.playerFacing: Two inspectors on a normal day and six when something has happened.
lore.gmOnly: The senior inspector is being quietly leaned on and is looking for a way out.

hooks: Something in a PC's bag cannot be explained in one sentence.
activities: Talk your way past an inspection.
Watch who else is being detained, and why.

cases.why: Declared standing, built as a scene: history and consequences are the two things depth 3 exists for, plus the deeper counts it owes (a third activity, a second NPC).

lore.summary: The one building big enough to feed several hundred candidates in three seatings.
lore.playerFacing: Trestle tables, a serving line, a noticeboard thick with drill schedules.
lore.gmOnly: The noticeboard is how the Directorate actually distributes bad news.

hooks: A notice goes up that changes somebody's posting.

cases.why: Depth 3 has no total-word ceiling on purpose: a place the group returns to all campaign is allowed to accumulate. This one is deliberately long and must not be flagged overweight.

lore.summary: The checkpoint everyone crossing to the island passes through, twice a day, for years.
lore.playerFacing: Eleven minutes when nothing is wrong and forty when it is. The barrier lanes move at different speeds and everybody has a theory about which.
lore.gmOnly: The permit system is being used to track movement, and nobody at the Transfer knows that.

hooks: A familiar face is missing from their post.
activities: Get something through that should not go through.
scene.history: Built with the causeway. The island line was added later and badly, which is why the transfer exists at all rather than a through service. During play it has been closed twice, both times without explanation.
scene.consequences: If the party is ever caught moving something through, inspections tighten for everyone and the queue times in every later scene here double.

cases.why: An unknown depth is refused rather than silently treated as named -- a typo in a declaration must not quietly downgrade what a location owes.
No depth declared at all defaults to named, the cheapest rung -- an undeclared location owes the least, not the most.

doc.name: Gate Post
doc.note: A booth and a barrier arm.

suggestCases.why: Content that already satisfies depth 2 while declared depth 0: suggestDepth reports the deepest rung it would pass, which is the promote-this signal.
